questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code authorizes access to orders and inventory? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
A warehouse user requests GET /orders/:id for an order whose status is pending. What response do they get?
choices: 200 with the order, because warehouse staff can read every order.
403 forbidden, because the policy denies the request.
404 not_found, because show? is false and deny_access reports show denials as not found.
404 not_found, because policy_scope hides the record before show? is evaluated.

questions.prompt: A support agent asks to refund 1,000 cents of a paid order whose refundable balance is 80,000 cents. What happens?
choices: 403 forbidden: the policy compares the order's whole refundable balance with the support limit, not the requested amount.
The refund succeeds, because 1,000 is below REFUND_LIMIT_CENTS.
422 invalid_amount, because the amount must equal the full refundable balance.
The refund succeeds only if the agent is also the order's owner.

questions.prompt: A customer sends PATCH /orders/:id for their own pending order with order[gift_note]=hello and order[internal_notes]=x (default Rails unpermitted-parameter handling). What is the outcome?
choices: 403 forbidden, because the request contains an attribute the customer may not set.
The order is updated including internal_notes, since update? is true for the owner of a pending order.
The order is updated with gift_note only; internal_notes is filtered out by permitted_attributes.
